artworks.title: Penelope, Laertes and Telemachus (BnF Français 874, fol. 3v)
artworks.description: A fifteenth-century French miniature in the Bibliothèque nationale de France gathers Penelope, aged Laertes and young Telemachus — the Ithacan household waiting while Odysseus wanders. Laertes appears as the retired king, grief and orchard still ahead of him in the Odyssey's last books.

artworks.title: Penelope, Laertes and Telemachus (BnF Français 874, fol. 8v)
artworks.description: Another leaf from the same BnF manuscript returns to Laertes with Penelope and Telemachus, the court of Ithaca imaged as a late-medieval family group. The illuminator keeps the father of Odysseus inside the homecoming story long before the orchard recognition.

artworks.title: Fragment of a Sarcophagus with Odysseus and Laertes
artworks.description: A Roman marble sarcophagus fragment in the Museo Barracco, Rome, shows Odysseus reunited with his aged father Laertes. The orchard recognition of Odyssey XXIV — scar, trees, and tears — becomes funerary relief, the nostos carved as a son's return to an old man among his vines.

films.title: Ulysses
films.description: Camerini's peplum keeps the aged father on Ithaca — Laertes' orchard reunion as the Odyssey's quiet homecoming coda.

popCulture.title: Laertes
popCulture.description: Odysseus' father endures as the retired king in the orchard — grief, recognition, and the last spear against the suitors' kin.
